strings.text: There is no glass here to collect.
strings.note: Toast (shown in capitals, one line) when the player collects a glass from a counter spot that has none. No slots.

strings.text: Collect the glass first — you cannot wipe under it.
strings.note: Toast when the cloth is used on a spot a glass still stands on. No slots.
Toast when the cloth is used on a spot with no mark. No slots.

strings.text: There is nothing in your hands to wash.
strings.note: Toast when the sink is clicked with no collected glasses in hand. No slots.

strings.text: The sink is running — wait for it.
strings.note: Toast when the sink is used while its tap is still running. No slots.

strings.text: That is not on this counter.
strings.note: Toast when a glass or mark that has already been cleared is acted on. No slots.

strings.text: The guest of the house is not yours to show the door.
strings.note: Toast when KICK is pressed on the story's guest. No slots.

strings.text: They are not waiting at the bar.
strings.note: Toast when serving, declining or kicking someone who is no longer seated and waiting. No slots.
Toast when KICK is pressed before the ID card was read. No slots.

strings.text: You cannot show the door to someone you have already served; the card was your moment.
strings.note: Toast when KICK is pressed on a customer who has already been served. No slots.

strings.text: They are not waiting any more.
strings.note: Toast when a serve or order change reaches a customer who has stopped waiting. No slots.

strings.text: The card has not been read; the papers are behind it.
strings.note: Refusal when the papers are asked for before the ID card was read. No slots.

strings.text: They are already at the bar.
strings.note: Refusal when a guest who is already seated is seated again. No slots.

strings.text: No drinks you can pour yet.
strings.note: Refusal when an order is rolled from a menu with nothing pourable. No slots.
Refusal when the last customer's trial is started twice. No slots.

strings.text: They have not asked for anything yet.
strings.note: Refusal when a drink reaches the story guest while they are still talking. No slots.
Refusal when a drink reaches the story guest after their trial ended. No slots.
Toast when a locked recipe is bought before its lock is met. {recipe} is the recipe's name (its data line); {lock} is the lock's label, one of the unlock.* lines (in capitals).
Toast when a recipe is bought without the cash. {recipe} is the recipe's name (its data line); {price} is the price with its currency sign, e.g. "$12".

strings.text: {fixture} is under the {lines}-line tower; take that one back first.
strings.note: Toast when a draught tower rung is refunded while a taller tower bought tonight stands on it. {fixture} is the fitting's name (its data line); {lines} is a number, the taller tower's line count.

strings.text: {fixture} is under a higher rung; take that one back first.
strings.note: Toast when a ladder rung is refunded while a higher rung bought tonight stands on it. {fixture} is the fitting's name (its data line).
Toast when a snack bowl with nothing left is served. {snack} is the snack's name (its data line).

strings.text: They are not at the bar.
strings.note: Toast when a snack is put down for someone no longer at the bar. No slots.

strings.text: Snacks ride a drink order — they have not ordered one yet.
strings.note: Toast when a snack is served to a customer who has not ordered a drink. No slots.

strings.text: Nobody is waiting on the last call.
strings.note: Refusal when the last-call plate's keys are used with no story guest tonight. No slots.

strings.text: Finish or bin the cocktail before you pull a pint.
strings.note: Refusal when the tap is pulled while the shaker holds a drink. No slots.

strings.text: There is already a drink in that glass — serve it or bin it before pulling a pint.
strings.note: Refusal when the tap is pulled into a glass holding another drink. No slots.

strings.text: The glass is full. Serve it or bin it.
strings.note: Refusal when the tap is pulled into a full glass. No slots.

strings.text: Nothing in the shaker to shake.
strings.note: Refusal when an empty shaker is shaken. No slots.

strings.text: Nothing in the shaker to stir.
strings.note: Refusal when an empty shaker is stirred. No slots.

strings.text: Two spirits in the tin — shake it or stir it before it goes to the glass.
strings.note: Refusal when an unmixed two-spirit tin is poured into the glass. No slots.
Toast when a drink is served to a customer who has not ordered yet. No slots.
Toast when serve is attempted with an empty glass and an empty shaker. No slots.

strings.text: That drink is still in the shaker — pour it into a glass first.
strings.note: Toast when serve is attempted while the drink is still in the shaker. No slots.

strings.text: They are still talking. Nothing ordered yet.
strings.note: Toast when a drink is served to the story guest during their dialogue. No slots.
Toast when an order is declined before the customer ordered. No slots.
Refusal when a market bottle already bought tonight is bought again. No slots.
Refusal when a stool is bought at the room's limit. No slots.

strings.text: The {glass} line is already the finest.
strings.note: Refusal when a glass line at its top tier is upgraded. {glass} is the glass's name (its data line).

strings.text: The bar top is already the best one.
strings.note: Refusal when the counter at its top tier is upgraded. No slots.
Refusal when a fitting the bar owns is bought again. {fixture} is the fitting's name (its data line).

strings.text: {fixture} needs a {stars}-star room; this bar rates {rating}.
strings.note: Refusal when a fitting is bought below its star gate. {fixture} is the fitting's name (its data line); {stars} and {rating} are ratings with one decimal, e.g. "2.0" and "1.5".

strings.text: {fixture} runs {lines} lines; this bar runs {bar_lines}. A tower is fitted one line at a time.
strings.note: Refusal when a draught tower is bought skipping a rung. {fixture} is the tower's name (its data line); {lines} is its line count; {bar_lines} is the bar's current line count (numbers).

strings.text: {fixture} is rung {level} of its ladder; the bar stands on rung {bar_level}. It climbs one rung at a time.
strings.note: Refusal when a ladder fitting is bought skipping a rung. {fixture} is the fitting's name (its data line); {level} is its rung number; {bar_level} is the bar's current rung (numbers).

strings.text: One fitting a night — the rest keeps until tomorrow.
strings.note: Refusal when a second fitting (stool, glass line, counter) is bought the same night. No slots.
Refusal when a purchase costs more than the till holds. {money} is the till and {price} the cost, each with its currency sign, e.g. "$8" and "$20".

strings.text: Perfect pour. Not a thing I would change.
strings.note: What a drinker says over a cocktail poured perfectly with nothing missing; speech line over the stool. No slots.
The short praise said before a missing-garnish complaint (advice.then). No slots.

strings.text: Pulled just right. Perfect head on it.
strings.note: What a drinker says over a perfectly pulled pint with nothing missing. No slots.
The short praise for a well-pulled pint said before a missing-garnish complaint (advice.then). No slots.
The smallest degree of a pour correction; fills {degree} at the start of advice.pour.* and advice.head.* (so capitalised).
The middle degree of a pour correction; fills {degree} at the start of advice.pour.* and advice.head.*.
The largest degree of a pour correction; fills {degree} at the start of advice.pour.* and advice.head.*.
Drinker's hint that an ingredient was over-poured. {degree} is advice.degree.*; {ingredient} is advice.ingredient.* or advice.type.* (lower case, e.g. "gin").
Drinker's hint that an ingredient was under-poured. {degree} is advice.degree.*; {ingredient} is advice.ingredient.* or advice.type.* (lower case, e.g. "tonic").
Drinker's hint that a pint has too much foam. {degree} is advice.degree.*.
Drinker's hint that a pint has too little foam. {degree} is advice.degree.*.
Two advice sentences said one after the other. {first} is a pour/praise sentence; {second} is advice.missing. Change the join (e.g. drop the space) where the language writes sentences differently.
Drinker's complaint that garnishes they ordered did not arrive. {garnishes} is one advice.garnish.* or a list built with advice.list.comma / advice.list.and.
Joins one more garnish onto a spoken list, before the last item. {list} is the list so far; {item} is advice.garnish.*.
Joins the last garnish onto a spoken list. {list} is the list so far; {item} is advice.garnish.*.

The draught preparation named out loud inside advice.missing (not normally a garnish).

Label under a locked shop/book item, capitals, no full stop. {stars} is the star rating wanted with one decimal, e.g. "2.5".
Label under an item earned from a story guest whose name is not known. Capitals, no full stop. No slots.
Label under an item earned by serving a story guest their order. Capitals, no full stop. {who} is the guest's name in capitals (a name, not translated).
Label under a keg held back until the bar's rank has opened enough draught lines. Capitals, no full stop. {lines} is a number (2 or 3).
Joins two lock labels when an item needs both. {first} and {next} are unlock.* labels (the first may itself be a join).
Calendar plaque and night slip. {week} is the week number; {night} is calendar.night.*. Capitals.

Preparation name (shaken in the tin); counter prop captions and tips. No slots.
One-line description of the shaken preparation, shown in a hover tip. No slots.
Preparation name (stirred with a bar spoon); counter prop captions and tips. No slots.

strings.text: Turned gently over a bar spoon.
strings.note: One-line description of the stirred preparation, shown in a hover tip. No slots.
Preparation name (served over ice cubes); counter prop captions and tips. No slots.

strings.note: One-line description of the mint garnish, shown in a hover tip. No slots.
Preparation name for a drink pulled from a keg. No slots.
One-line description of the draught preparation, shown in a hover tip. No slots.
Hometown printed on an ID card for a person with no town of record (shown in capitals on the card's citizenship line). No slots.
Hometown printed on an ID card. {town} is the town's name as the data file wrote it (a place name, not translated); leave as {town} unless the language wraps place names.

strings.text: The counter is repainted with the refinish kit — this bar does not own one yet.
strings.note: Refusal when the counter is repainted before the refinish kit (a one-time market upgrade) is bought. No slots.

strings.text: No bar spoon behind this bar yet — the first stirred recipe brings it.
strings.note: Refusal when the tin is stirred before the bar owns a bar spoon (the spoon comes with the first stirred recipe bought). No slots.

strings.text: The door is not yours yet — reach one star.
strings.note: Refusal when KICK is pressed before the ladder's second rung (1.0 star) has opened the door. No slots.
Refusal when a preparation the ladder has not opened is put on a glass: ice and the lemon twist come at half a star, the salt and sugar rims at one. {what} is the preparation's name, e.g. "Salt rim".

strings.text: No {what} in the house; the market sells the jar.
strings.note: Refusal when olives or mint are put on a glass before their jar has been bought in the market. {what} is the garnish name (Olives, Mint Sprig). Capitals as written, ~50 characters.
